headline: The new gift card purchase would charge customers one hundredth of the price, so it should not ship yet.
what_changed: Adds a gift card purchase feature in the code. No screen or customer page uses it yet, so no one has been charged.
Gift cards are offered at $25, $50 and $100.
Each purchase charges the buyer and creates a random 16-character code meant to be given to the recipient.
The project's README gets a short note describing the gift card purchase.

risks.title: Gift cards would charge one hundredth of their price
risks.explanation: Gift card prices are stored in dollars, but the payment step reads the number as cents. A $25 card would charge 25 cents, and a $100 card would charge $1. Nothing calls the feature yet, so no customer has been charged. If it goes live as written, the business would collect a tiny fraction of each sale, and receipts would not match what customers saw. The fix is to convert dollars to cents before charging, and to add a test that checks the amount.

risks.title: Gift card codes are never saved, so buyers may pay for nothing
risks.explanation: The purchase step creates the code and hands it back, but nothing stores it. No redemption step exists in this project either, so a code could not be used even if the buyer received it. If the feature went live without that work, customers would pay for a card they could not use. Save each code with its purchase record before the charge is made, and build redemption before launch.

risks.title: A timed-out payment could charge a buyer with no code issued
risks.explanation: The payment call gives up after 8 seconds. If the card is charged but the reply is lost, the purchase fails and the new code is thrown away, leaving a charge with no record to match it to. The duplicate-charge safeguard uses a code generated fresh on each attempt, so a manual retry would not be blocked and could charge the buyer twice. Use a stored purchase record and a stable reference per purchase, and check the gateway before retrying.

questions_for_developer: Is the gift card price in the catalog meant to be dollars? Please confirm that a $25 card sends 2,500 to the payment service, and fix the conversion before launch.
Where will each gift card code be stored, and how will a customer redeem it at checkout? Is redemption built anywhere else?
If a payment times out after the card was charged, how will we find that charge and give the buyer their code? Should we save a purchase record before charging?
Will the recipient get an email with the code? If so, does the email check the address and respect people who have opted out of emails?
good_news: Nothing customer-facing uses the feature yet, so no customer has been charged wrongly.
The change is small and contained: two new files and a short note in the README.
The existing payment code already expects amounts in cents, so the fix is one contained conversion.
